freshness.policy: Change-driven: any newer cited source review invalidates the question snapshot. No calendar-based expiry; re-retrieve and independently review after documentation/taxonomy changes. Fresh is relative to checked-in evidence, not a claim of perpetual correctness.

sources.title: Study Guide for Exam DP-700: Implementing Data Engineering Solutions Using Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: Authoritative DP-700 objective taxonomy effective July 21, 2026. The three domains each have a 30–35 percent weight. Used for taxonomy rather than as sole technical evidence.

sources.title: Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate
sources.shortSummary: Certification context for the Fabric Data Engineer Associate credential. Dynamic skill content returned Loading placeholders; implementation claims are grounded elsewhere.

sources.title: Implement data engineering solutions using Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: Instructor-led DP-700 course context. Dynamic sections were incomplete, so self-paced paths and modules were retrieved separately. Not used to prove technical answers.

sources.title: Configure high concurrency mode for Fabric notebooks
sources.shortSummary: Interactive high-concurrency sessions are enabled in workspace Spark settings. Sharing requires the same user and workspace, compatible default lakehouses, matching compute, and matching library packages; notebooks with no default lakehouse can share with each other.

sources.title: Data Engineering workspace administration settings in Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: Workspace admins configure pools, environment defaults, job admission, interactive expiry, high concurrency, and item compute customization. Maximum job lifetime cancels eligible user-submitted jobs but excludes system-managed maintenance, materialized lake view refreshes, and platform operations.

sources.title: Fabric CI/CD concepts and best practices
sources.shortSummary: Commit to Git exports supported item definitions and Update from Git applies branch definitions to workspaces. Feature branches paired with feature workspaces support reviewed integration, while deployment stages promote changes through environments whose configuration and permissions must be managed independently.

sources.title: Secure your Fabric Data Warehouse
sources.shortSummary: Warehouse access combines Fabric connectivity permissions with granular SQL authorization. Item Read is the minimum connectivity grant; object, row, and column security restrict different data scopes, and user audit activities identify actions on Fabric items.

sources.title: Dynamic data masking in Fabric Data Warehouse
sources.shortSummary: Masks modify result exposure rather than stored values and do not prevent inference through arbitrary predicates. Email masks use a fixed format; changing masks requires ALTER ANY MASK and table ALTER, while UNMASK or CONTROL permits original values. Workspace Admin, Member, and Contributor inherit CONTROL.

sources.title: SQL granular permissions in Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: GRANT, DENY, REVOKE, and SQL roles support granular authorization. Explicit CREATE USER is unavailable; GRANT or DENY creates the principal. SQL permissions can be staged before Fabric connectivity. Explicit catalog grant queries exclude permissions inherited from Fabric roles/items; effective permissions can be inspected with sys.fn_my_permissions.

sources.title: Parameters for Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: Pipeline parameters accept invocation values and remain fixed throughout a run, including when referenced in expressions. The reference defines pipeline system variables and string/conversion functions, including concat and coalesce, which returns the first non-null argument.

sources.title: Microsoft Fabric decision guide: copy activity, Copy job, dataflow, Eventstream, or Spark
sources.shortSummary: The comparison distinguishes lightweight pipeline copying, Power Query-based Dataflow Gen2, low-code Eventstreams, and code-based Spark. Spark offers notebooks, Python and other Spark languages, and native/open-source library support.

sources.title: Respond to Fabric events with Activator
sources.shortSummary: Fabric job events can drive Activator rules scoped to an item and outcome. Actions include Teams notifications and running Fabric activities such as cleanup notebooks. Scheduled-failure emails do not execute follow-up actions, and retriggering unchanged code/schema failures does not repair them.

sources.title: Fabric domains
sources.shortSummary: Domains group workspace items for business-oriented discovery without granting item access. Domain contributors require Admin on workspaces they assign. Default domains preserve existing assignments and cover unassigned and future workspaces for selected admins; bulk assignment is an existing-workspace action. Cited questions do not use Preview assignment-override settings.

sources.title: OneLake shortcuts
sources.shortSummary: The Caching section places supported external-shortcut cache configuration in workspace OneLake settings. Reset clears all cache files for that workspace. File access resets retention, and newer remote versions are fetched and update the cache rather than being pinned until expiry.

sources.title: Apache Airflow Job workspace settings
sources.shortSummary: Airflow starter pools stop after inactivity; custom pools remain on until paused and support node-size, autoscale, and extra-node configuration. Small is suggested for simpler DAGs, Large for complex/production DAGs, and each extra node supplies capacity for three additional workers.

sources.title: Spark compute configuration settings in Fabric environments
sources.shortSummary: A workspace admin gates per-environment compute overrides through Customize compute configurations for items. Runtime changes need save and publish, with compatible libraries and compute. Application-level spark.conf.set properties are distinct from environment compute configuration.

sources.title: Git integration for Fabric warehouse development
sources.shortSummary: Preview Warehouse Git integration stores schema as a database project of SQL files, excludes XMLA metadata, and commits at warehouse-item granularity. SQL permissions need separate handling; SQL analytics endpoint version control is unsupported. Warehouse reference cycles block branching/sync, and mismatched-collation lifecycle workflows can succeed yet leave inconsistent metadata.

sources.title: Deploy a warehouse using pipelines
sources.shortSummary: Preview warehouse pipelines use DacFx schema models; Compare requires a warehouse baseline in both workspaces. Defaults block possible data loss, exclude users/logins/permissions, omit database-option and transactional-DDL scripting, and retain target-only objects. A successful deployment can skip a requested table drop.

sources.title: Basic concepts in Git integration
sources.shortSummary: Fabric item/workspace authorization and repository authorization both govern Git operations. For Azure Repos, update requires Read while commit also requires Contribute and a permissive branch policy. Disconnecting the workspace requires Admin. The cited question satisfies item prerequisites and does not test the future-dated December 2026 policy notice.

sources.title: Roles in workspaces in Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: Workspace roles govern collaboration and execution. Viewer reads pipeline/notebook content and output but cannot execute or edit them. Multiple and nested group memberships supply the highest granted permissions. Admin, Member, and Contributor can execute notebook jobs, including API-driven execution.

sources.title: Column-level security in Fabric Data Warehouse
sources.shortSummary: SQL column-level grants restrict access at the database tier. The example grants a selected list of columns and demonstrates that SELECT * fails when it includes an ungranted confidential column rather than silently removing or masking that field.

sources.title: Endorse Fabric and Power BI items
sources.shortSummary: Owners or writers can promote useful items. Certification and master-data designation require authorized reviewers with write permissions. Master data specifically denotes core single-source-of-truth data and applies to data-containing items, unlike general promotion or quality certification.

sources.title: Domain-level default sensitivity labels in Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: The Preview domain-default-label setting applies labels on specified create/update/save events. Existing manual labels are preserved at any priority; lower-priority automatic labels can be replaced while higher-priority automatic labels are retained. Git and deployment pipeline support is currently excluded.

sources.title: Information protection in Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: Sensitivity-label access control depends on policy and access path. Labels associated with publishing policies can protect supported Power BI exports such as Excel and PDF; CSV/TXT and other unsupported export paths do not retain this documented protection. The article also distinguishes in-tenant protection policies from publishing-policy export protection.

sources.title: How OneLake security controls data access
sources.shortSummary: OneLake uses additive Grant roles, with object/row/column constraints intersected within a role and access unioned across roles. RLS combines with OR; SQL analytics endpoints instead intersect CLS allow lists. Folder grants inherit downward and permit ancestor traversal without sibling access. ReadWrite cannot contain RLS/CLS; DefaultReader may supply broad inherited access; unfilterable storage requests are blocked.

sources.title: Track user activities in Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: Fabric activity audit searches identify actions on items through Microsoft Purview or PowerShell. The Fabric guidance names Exchange Online's Audit Logs role as an access prerequisite, separate from workspace administration. Combined search filters constrain results and displayed times are UTC.

sources.title: Run, schedule, or use events to trigger a pipeline
sources.shortSummary: Scope of this record is fixed scheduling and storage-event expressions, not the article's Preview interval subsection. Scheduled parameter names must match definitions exactly; mismatches are ignored. Storage-event file names are accessed through a documented null-safe expression because manual runs lack event values.

sources.title: Run, schedule, or use events to trigger a pipeline
sources.shortSummary: Scope of this record is interval-based schedules, explicitly Public preview in the article. They provide nonoverlapping windows and window parameters, but native time-slice monitoring/backfill is unavailable, and interval schedules must be deleted/recreated rather than edited, enabled, or disabled.

sources.title: NotebookUtils notebook run and orchestration
sources.shortSummary: NotebookUtils run returns the child's exit string; exit must not be swallowed by exception handling and numeric consumers should convert the result. runMultiple DAGs separate activity names from notebook paths, dependencies refer to activity names, concurrency is a parallelism cap, and validateDAG catches cycles and missing references.

sources.title: Transform data by running a notebook
sources.shortSummary: Pipeline Notebook activities can authenticate with a Workspace Identity created in the pipeline workspace. The required API tenant setting must be enabled, and cross-workspace execution requires that identity to have at least Contributor access to the notebook workspace. Cross-region notebook calls are unsupported.

sources.title: How to implement dynamic data masking in Fabric Data Warehouse
sources.shortSummary: The implementation guide provides complete ALTER TABLE / ALTER COLUMN ADD MASKED syntax for email(), plus mask removal and privilege-sensitive testing. The cited candidate uses only this syntax evidence, not the guide's sample identities or data.

sources.title: Query acceleration for OneLake shortcuts - overview
sources.shortSummary: Explains external Delta caching/indexing, appropriate high-frequency OneLake query scenarios, storage costs, external-table limitations, and handling changes to advanced Delta features.

sources.title: Query acceleration over OneLake shortcuts
sources.shortSummary: Defines acceleration’s cache period relative to modificationTime in the Delta log rather than a business event-time column.

sources.title: arg_max() (aggregation function)
sources.shortSummary: Explains returning columns from the row maximizing an expression, grouped selection, and the difference from returning only a maximum scalar.

sources.title: avg() (aggregation function)
sources.shortSummary: Defines KQL arithmetic mean over non-null values, which determines the proper observation-count weighting when combining batch summaries.

sources.title: BETWEEN (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: Defines inclusive BETWEEN boundaries and inequality operators for exclusive bounds in T-SQL, including applicability to Fabric Warehouse.

sources.title: bin()
sources.shortSummary: Documents rounding existing values into bins and adding synthetic zero-valued bins to produce complete time-series output.

sources.title: Binary format in Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: Documents as-is unparsed Binary copying, the requirement for Binary on both ends, supported storage connectors, and optional compression.

sources.title: Use change data feed with Delta tables
sources.shortSummary: Documents enabling Delta CDF, retained version-based streaming reads, initial snapshot behavior, and insert, update_preimage, update_postimage, and delete metadata.

sources.title: How to copy data using copy activity
sources.shortSummary: Documents explicit source-to-destination column mappings and distinguishes assigning new-table column names from mapping into existing destination columns.

sources.title: COUNT (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: Defines COUNT(*) row counts, expression non-null counts, and distinct non-null counts; explicitly applies to Fabric Warehouse.

sources.title: Ingest data into your Warehouse using Transact-SQL
sources.shortSummary: Documents CTAS and SELECT INTO for new persisted Warehouse tables, SELECT-based transformations, and INSERT SELECT for already-existing tables.

sources.title: Dimensional modeling in Microsoft Fabric Warehouse: Dimension tables
sources.shortSummary: Explains surrogate versus natural keys, flattened and snowflake dimensions, attribute-specific historical change, and SCD type 2 version-level fact relationships.

sources.title: Microsoft Fabric decision guide: copy activity, Copy job, dataflow, Eventstream, or Spark
sources.shortSummary: Compares batch copy, dataflow Power Query preparation, no-code live Eventstreams, and code-based Spark. Used for authoring-fit decisions rather than broad claims that one engine is always superior.

sources.title: Eventhouse overview
sources.shortSummary: Describes Eventhouse as an engine for event, time-series, semistructured, and free-text analytics with KQL databases. Only engine-purpose sections are used.

sources.title: Process event data by using the event processing editor
sources.shortSummary: Documents the no-code event processing editor and supported preingestion destinations, including Lakehouse.

sources.title: Process events by using a SQL operator
sources.shortSummary: Documents Eventstream SQL tumbling/hopping windows, multiple output queries, event-time selection and lateness thresholds, and topology restrictions. Preview status is established by the separately fetched Eventstreams overview.

sources.title: Overview of Microsoft Fabric eventstreams
sources.shortSummary: Mixed-status overview: defines no-code event operators and routing, and explicitly marks the SQL operator Preview in Process events. GA no-code questions and Preview SQL questions are labelled individually; unrelated DeltaFlow and Spark Notebook previews are not tested.

sources.title: mv-expand operator
sources.shortSummary: Explains element-level row expansion, repeated unexpanded columns, null padding for parallel arrays, and Cartesian products from sequential expansions.

sources.title: has operator
sources.shortSummary: Defines case-insensitive whole-term matching and contrasts it with case-sensitive whole-term matching. Supplies a deterministic basis for evaluating the original message choices.

sources.title: Incrementally load data from Data Warehouse to Lakehouse
sources.shortSummary: Documents a change-increasing watermark, an exclusive old/inclusive new interval, and saving progress after successful copy. It does not make unchanged identifiers detect edits or handle arbitrary deletes.

sources.title: Create OneLake shortcuts in a KQL database
sources.shortSummary: Documents OneLake shortcuts in KQL databases as external tables queried with external_table rather than native ingested tables. Ordinary automatic schema sync is outside the candidate claims.

sources.title: Dimensional modeling in Microsoft Fabric Warehouse: Load tables
sources.shortSummary: Describes disposable staging reloads, dimensional transformations, preserving generated dimension keys, SCD processing, inferred members, soft deletion, and historical fact-version lookups.

sources.title: lookup operator
sources.shortSummary: Documents KQL fact-to-dimension lookup, the smaller right-side broadcast assumption, composite equality rules, and leftouter versus inner unmatched-row behavior.

sources.title: What is Mirroring in Fabric?
sources.shortSummary: Separates database replication, metadata-only catalog mirroring through shortcuts, and open mirroring. Only GA mechanisms and the listed Azure Databricks metadata case are used, not preview source connectors.

sources.title: Microsoft Fabric decision guide: Choose a data movement strategy
sources.shortSummary: Compares mirrored read-only replicas, controllable copy ingestion, and continuous Eventstreams. Questions use the documented read-only destination distinction and avoid universal pricing or connector claims.

sources.title: OneLake shortcuts
sources.shortSummary: The read deletion section distinguishes removing a shortcut object from deleting target files or folders through an authorized shortcut.

sources.title: parse_json()
sources.shortSummary: Documents dynamic pass-through versus string parsing and the need for tostring before parsing an embedded JSON string a second time.

sources.title: PySpark basics
sources.shortSummary: Documents portable static PySpark DataFrame projection, distinct rows, null handling, joins, and grouped aggregates. Only standard Spark APIs are used; no Databricks-specific catalog or runtime behavior is imported.

sources.title: Use Python for Apache Spark
sources.shortSummary: Establishes built-in PySpark support in Fabric notebooks and Spark jobs, making the standard DataFrame reference applicable to Fabric.

sources.title: range operator
sources.shortSummary: Documents generating a single-column table with an inclusive stop bound, datetime/timespan parameters, and union of generated time ranges.

sources.title: Shortcuts in a lakehouse
sources.shortSummary: Contrasts references with physical copies, Tables registration of Delta data with Files access, and circumstances requiring local materialization. Questions avoid the page’s simplified identity description.

sources.title: Overview of Structured Streaming
sources.shortSummary: Documents sources, sinks, microbatch execution, compatible-checkpoint recovery, and source/sink-dependent delivery guarantees. Preview or runtime-specific execution modes are not tested.

sources.title: Common Structured Streaming patterns
sources.shortSummary: Compares fan-out patterns and documents foreachBatch at-least-once behavior, per-table idempotent Delta transaction options, and the absence of group atomicity across sinks.

sources.title: Stateful processing with Structured Streaming
sources.shortSummary: Documents event-time windows, one-sided watermark guarantees, stream-join bounds, slow-input watermark behavior, and logical-ID deduplication within a supported watermark horizon.

sources.title: Microsoft Fabric decision guide: Choose between Warehouse and Lakehouse
sources.shortSummary: Compares Warehouse and Lakehouse by structured/unstructured data, Spark and SQL authoring, multi-table transactions, and read-only Lakehouse SQL serving.

sources.title: summarize operator
sources.shortSummary: Documents grouped output grain, empty grouped input, aggregate defaults, and null handling in KQL. Supports rollup and missing-bucket reasoning.

sources.title: Update policy overview
sources.shortSummary: Documents native-table ingestion triggers, same-database and schema prerequisites, transactional failure behavior, and zero-retention pass-through sources. Fabric-specific sections are used rather than Azure Data Explorer-only identity configuration.

sources.title: Respond to Fabric events with Activator
sources.shortSummary: Activator job events, available actions, and the distinction from centrally managed scheduled-failure emails.

sources.title: Monitor Copy activity
sources.shortSummary: Copy run diagnostics distinguish byte counts, row counts, effective concurrency, and changing execution-detail internals.

sources.title: Copy activity performance with SQL databases
sources.shortSummary: SQL-source copy tuning distinguishes requested and effective concurrency, source saturation, partition strides, and Warehouse staging.

sources.title: View refresh history and monitor your dataflows
sources.shortSummary: Dataflow refresh tables versus destination activities, Mashup logs, and save/validation versus runtime failures.

sources.title: Dataflow refresh
sources.shortSummary: Dataflow refresh cancellation effects, staging artifact identity issues, throttling, and Dataflows-connector timeout workaround.

sources.title: Workspace monitoring for Dataflow Gen2 in Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: CI/CD-enabled Dataflow Gen2 ItemJobEventLogs schemas, terminal statuses, refresh/publish separation, and alert queries.

sources.title: Optimize Delta Lake tables with V-order
sources.shortSummary: V-order write costs, file-level scope, selective writer configuration, and unchanged existing files after property changes.

sources.title: Manage and monitor an eventhouse
sources.shortSummary: Eventhouse overview tiles distinguish ingestion volume, database query activity, compute duration, storage, and schema changes.

sources.title: Change data policies
sources.shortSummary: Retention removes data; hot caching accelerates reads with a storage-cost tradeoff and cannot exceed retention.

sources.title: Monitor the status and performance of an eventstream
sources.shortSummary: Node-specific Eventstream metrics and runtime logs distinguish deserialization, conversion, and processing failures.

sources.title: Configure settings for a Fabric eventstream
sources.shortSummary: Eventstream throughput is constrained by source partitioning; changes require node/client coordination and lab results are not guarantees.

sources.title: Eventstream workspace monitoring overview (preview)
sources.shortSummary: Preview Eventstream monitoring schemas, emission intervals, and Max versus Sum metric aggregation.

sources.title: Use the Microsoft Fabric monitoring hub
sources.shortSummary: Monitoring hub historical durations, run details, and scheduled-failure notification configuration.

sources.title: .show ingestion failures command
sources.shortSummary: Read-only ingestion-failure command scope, 14-day retention, failure details, and permanent/transient classification.

sources.title: Best practices for Kusto Query Language queries
sources.shortSummary: Selective dynamic-field prefiltering, large-join shuffle strategy, and reducing repeated query work.

sources.title: Query limits
sources.shortSummary: KQL result truncation affects row count, byte size, and remote subqueries; explicit limits override notruncation.

sources.title: Shortcuts in a lakehouse
sources.shortSummary: Shortcut references, Files versus Tables discovery, and constraints on local table maintenance.

sources.title: Run Delta table maintenance in lakehouse
sources.shortSummary: Lakehouse Delta OPTIMIZE, optional V-order, VACUUM retention, and concurrent-reader/time-travel risks.

sources.title: Ingestion mappings
sources.shortSummary: Identity and explicit ingestion mappings, case-sensitive named fields, and mismatch symptoms.

sources.title: materialize()
sources.shortSummary: Query-scoped materialize reuse, shared per-node cache limit, semantic filter pushdown, and benchmarking cautions.

sources.title: Monitor materialized views
sources.shortSummary: Materialized-view age, permanent disabling, transient retries, failure inspection, and memory/cold-cache diagnosis.

sources.title: Native execution engine for Fabric Data Engineering
sources.shortSummary: Native execution plan markers, automatic fallback, and format/runtime limits; overview still explicitly mentions preview.

sources.title: Troubleshoot pipelines for Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: Documented common and Web activity error messages, supported connection types, missing properties, and response-size limits.

sources.title: Data refresh in Power BI
sources.shortSummary: Semantic refresh attempts, sequential independent Data/Query Cache phases, warnings, and refresh-detail monitoring.

sources.title: OneLake shortcut security
sources.shortSummary: Shortcut-path and target-path permission intersection, passthrough identity, and explicit delegated-engine exceptions.

sources.title: Troubleshoot Spark memory and performance issues
sources.shortSummary: Diagnoses Spark executor exits, skew, driver collection, cache pressure, Python process memory, and session-launch configuration.

sources.title: Spark monitoring and performance optimization best practices
sources.shortSummary: Spark run-series and same-item comparison correlate duration, input volume, configuration drift, and execution context.

sources.title: SQL analytics endpoint performance considerations
sources.shortSummary: SQL metadata synchronization, file-level scan parallelism, excessive partitioning, and maintenance impacts.

sources.title: Statistics
sources.shortSummary: Automatic and manual single-column statistics maintenance and the query latency of synchronous updates.

sources.title: Transactions in Fabric Data Warehouse
sources.shortSummary: Warehouse table-level write conflicts, schema locks, retry guidance, and statistics surviving rolled-back inserts.

sources.title: T-SQL surface area in Fabric Data Warehouse
sources.shortSummary: T-SQL endpoint differences and unsupported operations, including SQL analytics endpoint DML and mixed system/user-table queries.

sources.title: Performance guidelines in Fabric Data Warehouse
sources.shortSummary: Warehouse cache confounders, statistics, string lengths, transactions, file layouts, and query metadata views.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Configure high concurrency mode says Workspace settings > Spark settings > High concurrency > "For notebooks" enables shared interactive sessions; jobs core reservation, session timeout, and Customize compute for items are documented as unrelated controls.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Independent evidence from the high-concurrency and workspace-admin-settings articles supports one defensible key.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Fabric CI/CD best-practices supports feature branches paired with feature workspaces, PR-approved integration branch, then deployment pipelines through dev/test/prod. Unreviewed dev edits, developing in prod, and permanent isolation bypass the required PR gate or violate isolation.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The article combines feature workspaces, integration branch review, and staged deployment; competing options violate stated requirements.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Secure your Fabric Data Warehouse says Read is the minimum item permission for connectivity, item permissions plus SQL grants give scoped least-privilege access, workspace collaboration roles are explicitly broad, and masking does not restrict object access.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Warehouse access model and item permissions directly support the item-Read + SQL grant scoped design.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Secure your Fabric Data Warehouse describes RLS as WHERE-predicate row restriction and CLS as column restriction. Masking article shows masks do not stop inference and are not authorization. A whole-table grant enforces neither territory nor commission scoping.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Warehouse security page names RLS/CLS as the row/column authorization mechanisms; masking article says masks are not authorization.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Masking article demonstrates a range-predicate SELECT that reveals masked salary between 99999 and 100001, and directs teams to use CLS/RLS/SQL granular permissions rather than masking as a confidentiality control. UNMASK contradicts the requirement to deny access.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The Security consideration section shows exactly this inference pattern and recommends granular authorization.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Secure your Fabric Data Warehouse and Track user activities both direct compliance investigation to Microsoft Purview / PowerShell audit activities. Permission views and role lists are current state, not history; mask definitions describe result obfuscation.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Both the warehouse security article and the audit article name Microsoft Purview + PowerShell as the documented investigation path.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Parameters for Data Factory says once set, a parameter's value stays the same throughout the run; the immutability rule is not conditioned on expression use. Activity outputs do not reassign named pipeline parameters, and design-time defaults do not reset mid-run.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Parameter and expression concepts directly states the throughout-the-run stability rule.
